findings.detected_pattern: api.get_stock(sku) called with one argument after signature change to get_stock(sku, warehouse)
findings.issue: PR 418 added a required warehouse parameter to api.get_stock (stock/api.py:5), but the only caller, sync() in stock/jobs.py:12, still passes only sku. Every call raises TypeError, so the nightly sync fails on its first SKU and produces no output.
findings.suggested_fix: Thread a warehouse argument through sync(), e.g. def sync(skus: list[str], warehouse: str) -> list[dict] and call api.get_stock(sku, warehouse). Update the sync() callers to pass the warehouse as well.

findings.detected_pattern: sku and warehouse passed unvalidated from HTTP-facing get_stock into repository.fetch f-string SQL
findings.issue: api.py is documented as HTTP-facing, and get_stock forwards sku and warehouse unchanged to repository.fetch, where repository.py:11 interpolates both into an f-string SQL query. Request-supplied values can therefore inject SQL. The f-string itself is covered by the single-file pass; this finding is the cross-module data flow that makes it reachable. The HTTP route that calls get_stock is not in the PR's changed files, so reachability depends on that route passing request input through.
findings.suggested_fix: Parameterise the query in stock/repository.py:11 (cursor.execute('SELECT qty FROM stock WHERE sku = %s AND warehouse = %s', (sku, warehouse))) and validate sku and warehouse at the API boundary in get_stock before calling the repository.
